title: Hiraia reference archive options

recommendation.primary: Create a private Cloudflare R2 Standard bucket dedicated to reference materials, separate from public hiraia-assets.
recommendation.second_copy: Keep an independent private Backblaze B2 copy of originals and acquisition evidence, with file versions retained and a scoped ingest key. If choosing only one new provider, B2 is the lower storage-cost option.
recommendation.why: The known archive is about 21.6GB. The operational simplicity of an existing R2 integration and immediate access outweigh tiny cold-storage savings. A second provider still costs cents per month at this size.
recommendation.cost_assumption: Existing R2 storage allowance unavailable; a new B2 account has its first 10GB available. Ordinary request costs remain zero only while R2 account request allowances have headroom. Excludes tax, version growth and remote-only collections.
recommendation.cold_storage_threshold: Revisit Deep Archive when immutable collections grow to multi-TB scale and long restore delays are acceptable. Do not put the active educational reference library there just to save cents.

inventory.method: Read-only recursive file-path count and stat bytes, without hash deduplication or rights review. Snapshot of these directories only; a concurrent agent can add small mapping files after this measurement.
inventory.pdf_scope_note: Peru-quechua contains 628 school-material PDFs. Peru-curriculum separately contains the official programme PDF and extracted text. Do not count a duplicate temporary curriculum PDF twice.
inventory.unmeasured_remote_scope: finetuning/reference-materials/lrmds/README.md records 24,975 DepEd modules on RunPod at /workspace/corpus/raw/deped-lrportal/. Remote size, availability and present backup status were not checked.
inventory.excluded_large_assets: Model weights, APKs, image packs and general training corpora are outside this reference-library estimate.
originals_priority: human corrections and mapping review records
inventory.derivative_policy: Retain derivatives when cheap, labeled with parent hash and extractor/version; never substitute them for source bytes. Published training sets and human corrections require their own immutable release manifests.

billing_assumptions.duration: Full representative month; Backblaze quoted per 30-day storage rate
billing_assumptions.b2_units: Estimates interpret advertised TB as decimal 10^12 bytes and use byte-hour proration. Provider storage totals and invoice rounding are authoritative.
billing_assumptions.r2_units: GB modeled as decimal per R2 unit definitions; storage/retrieval round up to whole GB and request charges to million-request billing blocks.
billing_assumptions.allowances: Free allowances belong to an account, not a bucket. No account billing or secrets were inspected.

providers.lock_and_versions: Use content-addressed keys and bucket locks. Locks can be removed by a bucket-configuration administrator. Native S3 versioning operations are not listed in the compatibility table; archive correctness must not depend on them.

providers.pitfall: A month with even a small upload and read-back triggers a $9 Class A block and a $0.90 Class B block, plus retrieval and storage; this follows the official rounding rule and its explicit 1,000-write example.

providers.lock_and_versions: Retains all file versions by default. Governance Object Lock plus a key lacking delete/bypass capability suits the archive. Enabling Object Lock itself is irreversible; choose intentionally. Compliance retention cannot be shortened.
providers.price_change_note: May 1, 2026 replaced $6/TB with $6.95/TB and removed ordinary API charges. Ignore stale marketing pages still quoting $6.

providers.notes: Restore to a temporary readable copy before GET; internet download and temporary Standard storage can dominate the storage bill.
Lowest storage rate here; long restore workflow, six-month minimum billing and internet egress make it unsuitable as the active reference library.

providers.egress: Free subject to monthly downloads not exceeding active stored volume under published Pay-Go terms.
providers.reason: The one-TB monthly minimum makes a ~22GB reference archive substantially more expensive than R2 or B2.

first_ingest_example.scope: All inventoried files, stored individually; duplicate bytes not yet eliminated.
first_ingest_example.r2_standard_increment_if_account_allowan: Account-total rounding decides the exact increment: this small batch crosses at most one extra $4.50 A block and one extra $0.36 B block. Zero additional cost if it fits already-paid blocks.
first_ingest_example.multipart_note: Largest measured object is 66548718 bytes, so a single PUT per file is feasible. An 8MiB-threshold uploader instead produces approximately 8475 upload operations, still well within one million. Extra HEADs/list prefixes/retries add requests; do not copy the public-release script unchanged.
first_ingest_example.verification: Download every uploaded object and recompute SHA256; successful PUT or HEAD byte count alone is not proof of a recoverable archive.

aws_common_costs.versions: Versioning and Object Lock are available; retained versions incur storage.

implementation_recipe: Create a dedicated private reference bucket; no public custom domain or r2.dev access. Keep the existing public release bucket separate.

Build an inventory before uploading: source URL, final download URL, publisher, document title, country, subject, grade, language/variety, edition date, fetched timestamp, bytes, SHA256, rights/usage status and parent hash for derivatives.

Use immutable keys such as objects/sha256/<first-two>/<sha256>.pdf. Keep a versioned manifest in Git and also upload that manifest with every snapshot. Preserve multiple editions as separate hashes; deduplicate identical bytes without losing multiple source attributions.

Use a dedicated archive uploader with bucket-scoped credentials. Its routine token cannot change retention/bucket settings; keep the administrator credential separate. For B2 omit deleteFiles and bypassGovernance capabilities from the ingest key.
Retain originals indefinitely by policy; configure locks to enforce that policy where appropriate. Copy newly added objects and snapshots, never mirror local deletion into the archive.
Verify the initial upload by full read-back SHA256. Restore into an empty directory without the source laptop; check every restored file against the manifest and record the result.

Copy verified originals and acquisition evidence to B2 under separate credentials. Restore samples quarterly and a complete snapshot annually or after changing archive tooling; define an owner and record last successful restore.

Keep copyrighted references private. A downloaded textbook is not automatically cleared for redistribution or model training; expose only approved materials, and keep training rights as an explicit manifest field.
Treat Git as the catalogue and pipeline record, not bulk storage. Keep both cloud-object locators and the manifest schema in the repository so another machine can restore the collection.

sources.facts: Storage, request blocks, free allowances, retrieval and egress.
Standard has no minimum duration; Infrequent Access has 30 days.
Locks prevent deletion/overwrite but a configuration administrator can remove rules.
Designed for eleven-nines annual durability, distinct from protection against deletion.
Supported S3 operations; bucket versioning operations are not listed. Do not assume S3 native version recovery.
Defines GB as 10^9 bytes and GiB as 2^30 bytes.
Current $6.95/TB/30-day storage, first 10GB free, three-times average storage free egress, excess $0.01/GB; ordinary A/B/C API calls free, special Class D charge.
Raises B2 from $6 to $6.95/TB; ordinary API transactions become free. Some other Backblaze pages still show $6.
Governance can be bypassed by specifically authorized keys; compliance retention cannot be shortened. Enabling bucket Object Lock cannot be reversed.
All file versions are retained by default unless deleted; lifecycle rules can remove older versions.
Billed on file bytes; old versions and duplicate copies count.
US East N. Virginia S3 Flexible Retrieval and Standard storage/request rates.
Deep Archive storage, PUT, standard/bulk restore requests and retrieval bytes.
100GB aggregate monthly free internet egress; US East first paid 10TB is $0.09/GB.
Flexible minimum 90 days; Deep Archive minimum 180 days; each archived object adds 8KiB billed at Standard plus 32KiB at archival rate.
Restore needed before GET; Flexible bulk normally 5–12h, standard 3–5h; Deep Archive bulk within 48h, standard within 12h.
S3 bills storage in binary GB (GiB). Temporary restored copies incur Standard storage alongside original archival storage.
Object Lock protects individual versions and requires S3 Versioning.
Current starting Pay-Go price $7.99/TB/month; pricing calculator uses base 2.
$7.99/TB/month in all regions for affected Pay-Go accounts.
Pay-Go one-TB minimum, 90-day minimum duration; free egress when monthly downloads do not exceed active storage.
